summary: The knowledge tier now actually produces knowledge: its adjudication pass had been dropping 100% of pending claims since it was enabled, and its three passes now run once a day on a clock that survives a restart instead of once every five minutes on one that did not.
details: Adjudication was reaching zero candidates. `pending()` dropped any claim that was seen once AND whose subject resolved to no entity — measured against the live database as 53/53 in one workspace and 7/7 in the other, with 60 candidates sitting `pending` at `attempts = 0` and the tier holding exactly one fact, written 2026-08-28. The drop is now a RANK: such claims are adjudicated last instead of never, and `max_adjudications_per_tick` does the cost bounding it was always the thing actually doing.

The filter was a closed loop, and the loop was in the design rather than in the code: a subject resolves only via `fact_entity`; entities are minted only from standing facts at degree >= 2; a standing fact needs an adjudication; an adjudication needed a candidate that survived the filter. The only door in was an exact-triple recurrence, which 21 §6.2 makes structurally unavailable by forbidding either pass from canonicalising — `raft` and `Raft` are two rows that each count 1. Across 61 candidates in nine days, recurrence occurred zero times.

`fact-adjudication` and `fact-entity-resolution` had no schedule entry at all. Both are watermark-free, so they inherited the bare 5-minute Dreamer tick — 21 runs in 24 minutes across three workspaces — while `config.toml`'s own comment claimed all three knowledge adaptors ran daily. Both are daily now, and that comment is corrected in place.

The three passes run at different PHASES (candidates on its watermark, adjudication at 06:00 UTC, entity resolution at 07:00), so a claim extracted in the morning is adjudicated the same day rather than the next. `dream_loop` dispatches adaptors concurrently with no ordering, so equal intervals alone would have left them coinciding.

A scheduled adaptor's last fire is now persisted in a new `dream_schedule_state` table instead of a `time.monotonic()` dict inside the loop's own frame. The dict reset on every restart and the next tick always fired, so a daily adaptor was really a per-deploy one — and because `nora_dream_run_total` counts runs and not their reason, a reset clock and an elapsed one produced identical metrics.

A third watermark-free adaptor, note-entity-resolution, was found on the same bare tick and is scheduled here too (08:00 UTC). It has been cheap only because it offers a name to the model when `similar_entities` finds a near-miss among EXISTING entities, and the entity table has been empty for exactly the bootstrap reason above — so opening the filter is what would have started it calling a model every five minutes per workspace.

A schedule hold is now counted as `nora_dream_skipped_total{reason="schedule"}`. Without it a schedule that holds correctly and one that has stopped firing entirely are the same series, which is the class of blindness that let the original bug run eleven days.
limitations: Opening the filter does not by itself make the tier produce good facts. Extraction still emits predicates that carry their own object (`releases_1.0_at_end_of_october = true`) and splits subjects on casing, and neither is addressed here.

A candidate the model returns NO verdict for is still never retired -- `_retire_candidates` settles only the triples that came back, so a silently omitted claim stays `pending` with `attempts = 0`. This branch adds `last_adjudicated_at ASC NULLS FIRST` so the queue at least ROTATES instead of starving its tail behind newly extracted rows, but the underlying gap (spec 5.1's negative cache covers the explicit `not_covered` verdict only) is not closed and needs its own decision.

`SqlEntityStore.promote` mints entities from OBJECT literals only -- a subject that never appears as some other fact's object never becomes a `fact_entity` row. So the demoted rank is inert for subject-only names today, and the bootstrap is narrower than 'degree >= 2 over standing facts' suggests.
The phase offsets are a deliberate gap, not a dependency: nothing checks that an upstream pass finished before the next starts. A candidate written after 06:00 UTC waits for the next day's slot.
A backwards wall-clock jump can re-fire a scheduled adaptor once. That is the accepted cost of slot arithmetic over an absolute instant, and it is rarer than the per-deploy refiring it replaces.

note-curation's fire time changes: it had no time of day under the elapsed-time clock, and now runs at 16:00 UTC (HK midnight). That is a choice made here rather than a default, and it belongs to the note tier's owner to revise.
